limits_note: THE ARBITRAGE DOES NOT EXIST, and Sia's own numbers show it precisely. A host earns the median $1.17/TB/mo; a renter pays $2-3/TB/mo for the same terabyte (the $3 figure includes 3x redundancy). So contributing N TB of disk buys you N x 1.17/3 = 0.39N TB of retail storage - you must contribute ~2.6x the disk you want to consume, and you must also lock collateral at '2-3x your base storage price' in SC, keep the machine online, and forward ports. Storing 20 TiB on Sia costs $60-70/mo, which means hosting ~51-60 TB of other people's data to break even.
reliability_note: Lose the data or fail a proof and the collateral is burned; a single drive failure is a total loss for that contract.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.

extras.agent_focus: Marketplaces and networks where storage or bandwidth is contributed by third parties for free or near-free. Two directions probed: (1) BUY side - can you consume contributed bandwidth/storage cheaply; (2) SUPPLY side - the arbitrage question, whether contributing a disk earns storage credit at better than the retail rate. Also research testbeds that hand out whole physical nodes with multi-TB local disk (CloudLab, Chameleon, FABRIC, Emulab) and community mesh networks (Guifi, Freifunk, NYC Mesh). Decided per candidate by computing 20 TiB stored + 1 TiB/day egress against that path's actual tariff.
